text_blocks.snippet: For individuals born in 1960 or later, the full retirement age for Social Security benefits is 67 years old. Those born before 1960 have a full retirement age between 66 and 67, depending on their birth year. While you can start collecting benefits at age 62, doing so before your full retirement age results in a reduced monthly benefit. Conversely, delaying benefits past your full retirement age can increase your monthly benefit up to age 70.
